# How to read

Under each question there is a `- [ ] A:` line.

- **Tick it without writing anything:** you agree with the proposal.
- **Tick it and add a detail:** you agree, with that detail.
- **Leave it unticked and write:** I revise the proposal.

Built tonight and open to change: watching together (0.5.0, a first version), voice
and video messages, emoji, YouTube search and previews (0.4.5). Not built: transcription
and GIFs, which need your answers first.

# 1. Watching together: how it works now

Each side plays the video in its own mpv, straight from the link (YouTube through
yt-dlp, or any file or URL both can open): nothing of the video goes between you, so
it is as smooth and sharp as watching alone, with sound. Joma only keeps play, pause and
position in step: whoever pauses, plays or seeks, the other follows; the one who started
sends where they are every 3 seconds, and the other seeks when more than 0.8 s apart or
plays 5 % faster or slower when 0.15–0.8 s apart. Messages go in the call when there is
one (fast), else as account messages (slower to arrive). Start it from a YouTube link's
card (**watch together**) or `joma watch-together <to> <url>`; the other gets **join**.

Verified in the nest with a clock video: both players showed the same frame after
play, after a seek from the one who joined, and after a pause.

- [ ] A:

# 1b. Since then (0.5.1, your request)

`@youtube <search>` posts five results everyone sees; sessions belong to the
conversation (groups included), with a queue, and every playback action passes when
half of the participants agree (two people both command). Not tested with three people
yet (needs a third test account in a group); the vote counting is unit-tested.

- [ ] A:

# 2. Watching together: what is next

Proposals, in order:

1. Talk while watching: start it from a call (it already rides the call when there is
   one); suggest headphones (the call's echo cancellation does not know the video).
2. Choose the video in Joma (the YouTube search popover gets a **watch together**
   button), and a queue: the next video starts for both.
3. Clocks: positions carry the sender's clock, assuming both machines are NTP-synced
   (they are on Omarchy by default). If not, Joma can measure the offset with a ping
   through the call.
4. A "host" mode that streams the video to a friend without mpv: not planned, for the
   reasons we discussed (redistribution, the host's upload).

- [ ] A:

# 3. Ads

mpv with yt-dlp shows no ads: in practice it is an ad blocker, against YouTube's terms.
Each side fetches its own copy, so nothing is redistributed. yt-dlp needs updating when
YouTube changes (`pacman -Syu`). An alternative that keeps ads (or uses Premium) would be
syncing the YouTube player in the browser, through an extension: much more work.

- [ ] A: keep mpv / do the browser later / other

# 4. Transcription of voice messages

Proposal: local, with whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli`, in the AUR and as a package on
Arch), a small model (`base` or `small`, multilingual, 150–500 MB) downloaded once on
first use after asking. A voice message gets **transcribe**; the text appears under it
and is kept in Joma's cache (not sent into the conversation). Runs on the CPU (the
display GPU stays alone); a one-minute message takes a few seconds with `base`.

Questions: automatic for every received message, or on click? Which language by
default (auto-detect works, Italian is forced better)? Send the transcript to the
conversation as well (useful for the other side), or keep it local?

- [ ] A:

# 5. GIFs

GIF search needs an API key: Giphy and Tenor both require one, tied to an account and
its terms. Proposals: (a) you create a Giphy key and set it in Settings; Joma searches
with it and sends the GIF as a file (so it plays in Jami too); (b) no search, but
pasting or dropping a GIF already works and shows animated in the conversation;
(c) a local collection: a folder of GIFs you keep, searchable by name.

- [ ] A: (a) / (b) / (c)

# 6. Voice messages in the test setup

Recording works with real devices; in the test profiles (silent ALSA null device) the
recorder spins and cannot be stopped, as calls do. Joma stops it off the UI thread, so
the window never freezes, but a test recording is never sent. Please try a voice
message on your machine and tell me whether it sends and plays on the other side.
